---
title: "Mixed models"
---

`fit_lmer()` fits Gaussian linear mixed models, as `lme4::lmer()` does.
`fit_glmer()` fits a binomial logit model with one random intercept, as
`lme4::glmer()` does for that structure. Both take an R formula with lme4's
bar syntax for random effects.

```php
Phit\fit_lmer(string $formula, array|object $data, bool $reml = true, string $missing = 'drop',
    array|string|null $weights = null, ?array $start = null, int $maxEvaluations = 20000,
    float $tolerance = 1e-7, string $optimizer = 'bobyqa', float $objectiveTolerance = 1e-12): array;
Phit\fit_glmer(string $formula, array|object $data, string $family = 'binomial', string $link = '',
    string $missing = 'drop', array|string|null $weights = null, int $quadraturePoints = 1,
    int $maxEvaluations = 20000, float $tolerance = 1e-7): array;
```

## Supported structures

| Function | Random terms | Family and link | Fitting method |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fit_lmer` | `(1 | g)`, `(x | g)`, `(0 + x | g)`, `(x || g)` (uncorrelated), several terms such as `(1 | g1) + (1 | g2)`, interaction groups `(1 | g1:g2)`, and nesting `(1 | g1/g2)` | Gaussian, identity | REML (default) or ML (`reml: false`); BOBYQA (default) or Nelder–Mead (`optimizer: 'nelder_mead'`) |
| `fit_glmer` | Exactly one `(1 | g)` | Binomial, logit | ML by Laplace (`quadraturePoints: 1`, the default) or adaptive Gauss–Hermite quadrature with 2 to 61 points |

Any other random-effect structure, family or link throws code 1007. Random
slopes, several random terms, the Poisson and probit families, and REML are
not available in `fit_glmer()`. Random-effect terms in `fit_lm()` or
`fit_glm()` also throw code 1007.

## A random-intercept model

The example uses `docs/data/schools.csv` from the repository: 250 simulated
students in 12 schools, with study hours, a prior score and a test score.

```php
use function Phit\{fit_lmer, read_csv};

$csv = read_csv('docs/data/schools.csv');
$schools = array_combine($csv['names'], array_column($csv['columns'], 'values'));

$fit = fit_lmer('score ~ study_hours + prior_score + (1 | school)', $schools);
foreach ($fit['columns'] as $i => $name) {
    printf("%-12s %8.4f %8.4f\n", $name, $fit['coefficients'][$i], $fit['std_errors'][$i]);
}
$school = $fit['random'][0];
printf("%s: school SD %.4f, residual SD %.4f, %d schools\n", $fit['method'],
    sqrt($school['covariance'][0][0]), $fit['sigma'], count($school['group_labels']));
printf("%s %+.4f\n", $school['group_labels'][0], $school['effects'][0][0]);
```

```
(Intercept)   46.6627   2.2438
study_hours    1.6141   0.1609
prior_score    0.2453   0.0419
REML: school SD 4.4579, residual SD 5.0566, 12 schools
school-01 +0.1353
```

`school-01`'s predicted random intercept is 0.14 points above the average
school.

## Reading a fit_lmer result

| Key | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `coefficients`, `std_errors`, `z_statistics`, `p_values`, `conf_int`, `covariance` | Fixed effects, with normal (Wald) tests and 95% intervals |
| `random` | One entry per random term, in formula order |
| `sigma`, `residual_variance` | Residual standard deviation and variance |
| `theta` | Relative covariance factors, as lme4's `getME(fit, "theta")` |
| `log_likelihood`, `aic`, `bic`, `n_parameters` | The REML criterion or the ML log-likelihood, according to `method` |
| `fitted`, `fixed_fitted`, `residuals`, `marginal_residuals` | Conditional and fixed-effects-only predictions and residuals |
| `method`, `optimizer`, `evaluations`, `converged`, `singular` | Fitting details |

Each `random` entry has `label`, `group`, `columns` and `correlated`, the
term's `covariance` matrix, `effects` (one row of conditional modes per group),
`effects_cond_var` (one k×k conditional covariance per group, lme4's
`ranef(condVar = TRUE)`), `group_labels` and `group_sizes`. Groups are ordered by
first appearance after missing-value deletion. lme4 sorts them instead. The
estimates do not depend on the order.

The fixed-effect tests use the normal distribution. lme4 reports t values
without p-values, and packages such as lmerTest add degrees-of-freedom
approximations. phit has no degrees-of-freedom correction.

## Singular fits

A random-effect variance estimated at or near zero, or a correlation at ±1,
makes the covariance singular. The fit returns with `singular` true and the
warning `random-effect covariance is singular or near singular` in
`diagnostics.warnings`. With these data, `score ~ study_hours + (1 +
study_hours | school)` is singular: the slope variance is about 0.001. A
singular fit usually means the random-effect structure is more complex than
the data support.

## A binomial random-intercept model

`docs/data/cbpp.csv` holds lme4's `cbpp` data: cases of contagious bovine
pleuropneumonia in 15 herds over four periods.

```php
use function Phit\{fit_glmer, read_csv};

$csv = read_csv('docs/data/cbpp.csv', ['types' => ['c', 'i', 'i', 'c']]);
$herds = array_combine($csv['names'], array_column($csv['columns'], 'values'));
$herds['healthy'] = array_map(fn ($n, $k) => $n - $k, $herds['size'], $herds['incidence']);

$fit = fit_glmer('cbind(incidence, healthy) ~ period + (1 | herd)', $herds, quadraturePoints: 10);
foreach ($fit['named'] as $name => $b) printf("%-12s %8.4f\n", $name, $b);
printf("herd SD %.4f, %s\n", $fit['random_intercept_sd'], $fit['integration']);
```

```
(Intercept)   -1.3992
period2       -0.9914
period3       -1.1278
period4       -1.5795
herd SD 0.6475, adaptive_gauss_hermite
```

`quadraturePoints` is lme4's `nAGQ`. The Laplace default is fastest. More
points approximate the likelihood more closely, which matters most for small
groups and rare events. No number of points guarantees accuracy for every data
set, so compare a few values when the estimates matter.

A `fit_glmer` result reports the herd effects directly: `random_effects`,
`random_effects_cond_var`, `group_labels`, `group_sizes`, `n_groups`,
`random_intercept_variance` and `random_intercept_sd`. It also has
`linear_predictor`, `neg2_log_likelihood`, `quadrature_points`, `integration`,
`gradient_max` and `boundary`, and the fixed-effect keys of `fit_lmer`.

## Prediction

`predict()` adds each known group's random effects by default, as lme4's
`re.form = NULL` does. `random: false` predicts at the population level, and
the grouping columns can then be absent. A group the fit never saw throws
code 1001 unless `allowNewLevels: true`, which predicts it at the population
level. Mixed-model predictions have no standard errors, as in lme4.

## Matrix functions

`fit_mixed()`, `fit_mixed_intercept()` and `fit_logistic_mixed()` fit the same
models from numeric matrices and explicit random-effect designs.
`fit_mixed_intercept()` is a faster path for a Gaussian random intercept by
ML. [Matrix model functions](reference-models.qmd) defines their inputs, the
optimizer controls and the convergence rules.
